parts.visual:
A P&L (Profit and Loss statement) shows a company's revenues and expenses during a specific period. If you can't read a P&L, you can't lead.

Key Components:
1. Top Line: Total Revenue (Money coming in).
2. COGS / OPEX: Costs and Operating Expenses (Money going out).
3. Bottom Line: Net Profit (What is left).
parts.audio: If you cannot read a Profit and Loss statement, you cannot lead. Master the Top Line, Operating Expenses, and the Bottom Line.

questions.question: What does it mean when a CEO says they want to focus on 'Top-Line Growth'?
options: They want to increase employee salaries.
They want to aggressively increase total sales and revenue, even if it requires spending more money to do so.
They want to buy a taller building.
questions.correct_answer: They want to aggressively increase total sales and revenue, even if it requires spending more money to do so.
questions.explanation: The 'Top Line' refers to the very first line of a P&L statement: Gross Revenue/Sales.

questions.question: Listen to the financial update. Which part of the P&L is being discussed?
questions.tts_text: We need to reduce our OPEX by 10% this quarter to maintain our margins.
questions.explanation: OPEX includes rent, payroll, and marketing—the costs required to operate the business on a daily basis.

questions.question: Why is 'Margin' often more important than total revenue?
options: Because you can have $10 Million in revenue, but if your costs are $11 Million, the business is dying. Margin is the percentage of revenue you actually keep.
questions.correct_answer: Because you can have $10 Million in revenue, but if your costs are $11 Million, the business is dying. Margin is the percentage of revenue you actually keep.
questions.explanation: Profit Margin is the true indicator of a company's health and pricing power.

questions.question: What is the 'Bottom Line'?
options: The physical bottom of the page.
Net Income; the total profit remaining after all expenses, taxes, and costs have been deducted from revenue.
The lowest acceptable price in a negotiation.
questions.correct_answer: Net Income; the total profit remaining after all expenses, taxes, and costs have been deducted from revenue.
questions.explanation: When an executive asks 'How does this affect the bottom line?', they mean 'Will this ultimately make or lose us money?'

pairs.match: Income generated from normal business operations
The difference between revenue and costs
